subtopics.title: The Concept and Causes of Market Failure

questions.question: Market failure is best defined as:
options: The market producing quantities different from the socially optimal ones, so a better allocation could raise society's welfare
Any situation where prices are high

questions.question: The market for streetlights never forms at all because:
options: Streetlights are too expensive to build
Non-rivalry and non-excludability mean no firm can charge users — a missing market, failure at its most absolute

questions.question: Miners in a dying coal town who cannot retrain or relocate illustrate which cause of market failure?
options: Immobility of factors of production — the standing South African case being structural unemployment

questions.question: "A market can be perfectly efficient and still leave a nation hungry" refers to:
options: Inequality — markets weight demand by purchasing power, so unmet needs backed by no money attract no resources

subtopics.title: Externalities — Private Against Social Costs and Benefits

questions.question: Social cost equals:
options: The price paid by the consumer

questions.question: On the polluting paper mill diagram, the marginal social cost curve:
options: Lies below the private cost curve
Runs parallel above the marginal private cost curve, the vertical gap being the external cost per ton

questions.question: The market equilibrium for the polluting good compared with society's optimum shows:
options: Smaller output at a higher price
Larger output at a lower price — the market over-produces and under-prices the polluting good

questions.question: Vaccination is under-produced by the market because:
options: Demand for vaccines is perfectly elastic
The market demand curve counts only the private benefit, ignoring the external benefit to everyone the vaccinated person never infects

questions.question: A tax set equal to the external cost per unit corrects a negative externality by:
options: Lifting the private cost curve onto the social cost curve, so the market itself chooses the smaller, socially optimal quantity

questions.question: South Africa's carbon tax, sin taxes and the sugary drinks levy are examples of:
options: Taxes on external costs — making the polluter or consumer pay the social cost

questions.question: A maximum price set below equilibrium for an essential good typically causes:
options: Shortages and queues — the standard side effect of holding price below the market-clearing level

questions.question: The evaluation point that completes any answer on the state's toolkit is:
options: Every instrument has a cost — wrong levels, financing burdens, distortions — and each intervention risks public sector failure, so each needs its own justification

questions.question: Public projects need cost-benefit analysis rather than market profit tests because:
options: Many of their costs and benefits are external, unpriced or decades away — profit measures only the private slice

questions.question: Future benefits are DISCOUNTED in CBA because:
options: Future benefits are always uncertain fabrications
A rand of benefit in twenty years is worth less than a rand today, so distant flows must be shrunk before adding
Discounting doubles the value of a project

questions.question: A high discount rate in a climate-related CBA effectively:
options: Has no effect on the outcome
Silences future generations by shrinking distant benefits toward zero — a moral choice disguised as arithmetic

questions.question: "A project can pass while hurting the poorest" warns that CBA:
options: Sums rands without asking whose they are — distribution must be judged alongside the total

questions.question: The honest cost of the R40 chicken is R45 because:
options: The village pays roughly R5 per chicken in boiled water, clinic visits and lost garden yield — a bill that never reaches the farm or buyer
The farm underpays its workers by R5

questions.question: Because chickens LOOK R5 cheaper than they truly are:
options: Fewer chickens are sold than society wants
People buy more of them than they would at the honest price — the market over-produces the harmful good

questions.question: The evening classes stay half-empty because:
options: Students pay for the whole benefit but capture only part of it — the village's share of the gain is not counted in anyone's decision to enrol
The classes have no external effects

questions.question: The one-sentence pattern of the riverbank is:
options: A missing bill makes too many chickens; a missing thank-you makes too few classes — external costs over-produce, external benefits under-produce

subtopics.title: Fixing the Price Until It Tells the Truth

questions.question: The R5 chicken levy is elegant because:
options: Government never orders the farm to do anything — it corrects the price and lets the market choose the smaller quantity itself

questions.question: Subsidising evening classes down to R20 is justified because:
options: Society keeps part of the benefit, so society pays for that part — the missing thank-you delivered

questions.question: "Poison has no correct price" argues that:
options: When harm is grave enough, regulation — an outright rule like no dumping near the river — beats merely taxing the behaviour

questions.question: "Good policy is choosing the smaller failure" means:
options: States always fail worse than markets
Markets always fail worse than states
Both markets and state fixes can fail, so each case must weigh the market's failure against the state's likely failure in correcting it

questions.question: The dam cannot be judged by market prices because:
options: Half of what matters — drowned fields, lost wetlands, prevented floods — carries no market price
Government projects are exempt from prices

questions.question: The wetland is valued in the CBA at:
options: At least what a treatment plant doing the same water-cleaning job would cost
The price of the land if sold

questions.question: When three projects compete for one budget, CBA ranks them by:
options: Benefit per rand — the benefit-cost ratio

questions.question: The two-line caution on CBA is:
options: It is always accurate and always fair
It should never be used for dams
Champions can game the counting, and the page adds rands without asking whose — so watch for optimism bias and ask about compensating the losers
